messages.subject: Optimizing stan code
parts:
Dear all,

I'm trying to convert my OpenBugs model in Stan. Among two ways of writing my model, I'm wondering wich one is the best. Here is an example:

code1:
...
for(i in 1:N)
   model {
         Z1[i] ~ normal(a*X[i] + b*Y[i] , tau)
         Z2[i] ~normal(a*Y[i] + b *X[i] , tau)
   }

or code2:
...
for(i in 1:N)
   model {
          for( j in 1:2) {
               Z[i,j] ~ normal(a*X[i,j] + b*Y[i,j] , tau)
           }
     }

Is it the same code, for the value "tau"?
Thank you.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Optimizing stan code
parts:
On 12/9/13, 6:19 AM, Leon-Alph wrote:

> I'm trying to convert my OpenBugs model in Stan. Among two ways of writing my model, I'm wondering wich one is the best.

You can always try both. But there are some general guidelines
in the chapter of the manuals on arrays vs. vectors/matrices.
And more below.

> Here is an example:
>
> _code1:_

> ...
> for(i in 1:N)
> model {
> Z1[i] ~ normal(a*X[i] + b*Y[i] , tau)
> Z2[i] ~normal(a*Y[i] + b *X[i] , tau)
> }
>

> ...
> for(i in 1:N)
> model {
> for( j in 1:2) {
> Z[i,j] ~ normal(a*X[i,j] + b*Y[i,j] , tau)
> }
> }

> Is it the same code, for the value "tau"?

I'm not sure what the type of X, Y, and Z1 are here, and
it looks like they're being used differently in (1) and (2).
Also, the "for" has to go inside the model.

Loops are cheap in Stan, but calls to probability functions
are not. So vectorizing the sampling statement is your
best bet. Rewriting your model 2 (so that the order of rows
and columns of Z is reversed and it uses an efficient array
of vectors representation):

vector[I] Z[2];
vector[I] X[2];
vector[I] Y[2];

Z[j] ~ normal(a * X[j] + b * Y[j], tau);

- Bob
